bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Foreign exchange volatility and global economic uncertainty — Management explicitly flagged global economic uncertainty and volatility in foreign exchange rates as continuing areas of attention for the Empire Machine Tools (EMT) division, which also relies partly on exchange-rate variation gains for profitability.
- Slow government-sector order finalisation — Order finalisation in government sectors (Defence, Aerospace) remains relatively slow for EMT due to multi-level approval processes associated with global tenders, creating uncertainty on the timing of order conversion despite 'Make in India'-driven order receipts.
- Prevailing market challenges in the glass packaging business — Vitrum Glass delivered stable performance during the year 'despite prevailing market challenges,' indicating an ongoing external demand/pricing pressure the division must continue to manage.
- Empire Industrial Equipment (EIE) still in a recovery phase — EIE 'continued its recovery phase' during the year, with several projects still under discussion or in execution stages rather than concluded, indicating the division's turnaround and revenue conversion is not yet complete.

business.body: Empire Industries Limited is a diversified conglomerate operating through four divisions: Vitrum Glass, which manufactures and markets glass bottles for the pharmaceutical industry in domestic and export markets; Empire Machine Tools (EMT), which supplies machine tools and value-added engineering/service contracts to sectors such as Energy & Power, Automotive, Defence, Railways, Steel and Aerospace; Empire Industrial Equipment (EIE), which supplies capital equipment and undertakes turnkey project execution for Oil & Gas, Steel & Metallurgy, Ports and Shipyards; and Empire Vending, comprising the Grabbit+ smart vending platform and the Emperia 1900 hygiene and cleaning products portfolio.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Vitrum Glass:** Glass bottles for pharmaceutical packaging (5 ml to 650 ml range)
- **Empire Machine Tools:** Machine tools, CAMC/AMC service contracts, value-added engineering services
- **Empire Industrial Equipment:** Capital equipment for Oil & Gas, Steel & Metallurgy, Ports and Shipyards, turnkey project execution
- **Empire Vending:** Grabbit+ smart vending machines/digital vending infrastructure, Emperia 1900 disinfectants, housekeeping products, kitchen care products, personal hygiene solutions

- Diversified, high-value and niche order book in Empire Machine Tools spanning Energy & Power, Automotive, Defence, Railways, Steel, Aerospace and Machine Tools

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Vitrum Glass: continued focus on operational efficiency, product quality and customer service to support improved performance
- Empire Machine Tools (EMT): continues to focus on Energy & Power, Automotive, Defence, Railways, Steel, Aerospace, Oil & Gas, Research Institutions and Machine Tools, with OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers as the primary customer base
- Empire Industrial Equipment (EIE): developing localized solutions under 'Make in India' by collaborating with Indian partners for fabrication, assembly and packaging while integrating overseas principal technologies
- Empire Vending (Grabbit+): expanding digital vending infrastructure, focus on cashless transactions, inventory management systems and data-driven operational efficiencies; expanding product offerings for workplace consumption and wellness trends
- Emperia 1900: expanding hygiene and cleaning solutions portfolio; introducing product improvements in operational safety, packaging durability and ease of handling; conducting hygiene/safety training for institutional customers; exploring sectors with rising hygiene/institutional cleaning standards
- Empire Industrial Centrum, Ambernath: evaluating launch of a commercial development within the 35-acre phased project
- The Empire Business Centre (TEBC): maintaining market presence through customer retention, broker relationships and digital outreach; continues to evaluate expansion opportunities in Mumbai and other business districts
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Empire Industrial Centrum at Ambernath is a 35-acre phased development that commenced in FY2014-15; Phases 1 to 7 are registered under RERA, with Phases 1-4 completed and occupation certificates received for all 9 buildings in these phases, while Phase 6 and Phase 7 (industrial) have subsequently been deregistered from RERA as registration is not mandatory for such projects. The project remains a long-gestation development and continues to benefit from infrastructure improvements in the surrounding region, including the ongoing construction of the proposed Chikhloli railway station near the project site; the Company expects improved sales momentum and collections in the coming years and is evaluating the launch of a commercial development within the project. The Empire Business Centre (TEBC) provides serviced and furnished office spaces at Lower Parel and Airoli, and continues to evaluate expansion opportunities in Mumbai and other business districts. The Empire Commercial Property division manages commercial and IT office spaces at Lower Parel and Vikhroli, Mumbai, comprising approximately one million square feet, including Empire Plaza 1 and Empire Plaza 2 at Vikhroli (full occupancy during the year) and the Empire Complex at Lower Parel (strong occupancy). Empire Foods, which imports frozen and chilled food products and distributes dairy and bakery products through twelve branch offices across India, launched CANDIA whipping cream and butter sheets for the bakery segment during the year and is evaluating the introduction of additional international brands in the Indian market. Company-wide capital expenditure for FY26 was on account of Plant & Machinery Rs. 376.66 Lakh (Rs.266.05 Lakh prior year), Vehicles Rs.366.91 Lakh (Rs. 237.68 Lakh), Office Equipment Rs.53.09 Lakh (Rs.122.19 Lakh), Furniture & fixtures Rs.5.46 Lakh (Rs. 1.25 Lakh) and Software Rs.43.73 Lakh (Rs. 5.40 Lakh).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's growing manufacturing base and increasing demand for advanced machine tools and niche technologies expected to support long-term industry growth for EMT
- Government of India's 'Make in India' initiative continued to support private sector participation in Defence and Aerospace, resulting in receipt of several strategic orders for EMT, though government-sector order finalisation remains slow due to multi-level approval processes for global tenders
- Ports & Shipyards, Steel & Metallurgy and Oil & Gas expected to remain key focus sectors for EIE in FY27, with encouraging industry investment trends
- Infrastructure improvements near the Ambernath project, including the ongoing construction of the proposed Chikhloli railway station, expected to support improved sales momentum and collections for Empire Industrial Centrum
- Increasing institutional focus on hygiene standards and cleaning requirements expected to create opportunities for Emperia 1900
- Increasing competition in the co-working and flexible office space sector noted as a demand backdrop for TEBC
- EMT recorded strong order inflows during the year across Energy & Power, Automotive, Defence, Railways, Steel, Aerospace and Machine Tools, with a diversified mix of high-value and niche projects; several 'Book and Bill' orders with advance payments supported cash flow
- EMT enters FY 2026-27 with a healthy order pipeline and expects continued business from existing customers, including orders with improved payment terms
- EIE has several projects remaining under discussion and in execution stages as the division continues its recovery phase
